title: Canadian skyrunner Kalie McCrystal goes missing during training run on Matterhorn
content:
Canadian skyrunner Kalie McCrystal is missing after going for a run on the Matterhorn in Italy this week.

An Athletics Canada statement said McCrystal, 38, of Squamish, B.C., was on a “reconnaissance/training session” in advance of an attempt at a “mountain-running record” on the famed peak and was last seen Tuesday.

“Kalie is an experienced skyrunner and mountaineer, with many years of experience in technical and high-altitude mountain environments,” the statement said. “She has extensive knowledge and experience of alpine terrain and had previously climbed the Matterhorn. This was therefore not her first ascent of the mountain.”

Athletics Canada said McCrystal’s family is continuing to work with mountain rescue services.

Amelia Boultbee, a close friend of McCrystal’s dating to their time together at law school at the University of British Columbia, described McCrystal as an “elite athlete” in “peak physical condition.”

“She’s a live wire,” Boultbee said in a phone conversation. “She’s a really fun person. She’s extremely focused. She’s very determined, really smart. She’s one of the most disciplined people you could ever meet, and yeah, we’re really worried about her.

“… I found out on Friday that Kalie was missing. I didn’t know right away, and ever since then, myself and all of her friends, we’re just trying to push the news out and ask for prayers for her safe return.”

Boultbee said McCrystal’s family is working with Italian authorities, trying to figure out when her phone last stopped receiving messages. She asked for anyone who “may have had contact” with McCrystal between 15:45 CET (9:45 a.m. EDT) Tuesday and 9:26 CET (3:26 a.m. EDT) Wednesday to reach out to her X account.

The Matterhorn rises to 4,478 meters (14,692 feet) on the border between Switzerland and Italy in the Pennine Alps.

McCrystal won the 4 Refugios Non-Stop race in Bariloche, Argentina, in February. She finished the nearly 40-kilometer course, which peaked at 3,350 meters (10,991 feet), in 6 hours, 21 minutes, 10 seconds.

According to the Fastest Known Time database, McCrystal successfully traversed the Matterhorn on the Hörnli Ridge round trip from Zermatt, Switzerland, in 6:47:33 on Aug. 14. She started from the Italian side Tuesday.

In her uploaded report on the Matterhorn run in August, McCrystal wrote that she briefly lost her way. “I intended this to be a recon run, but ended up faster than I thought,” she wrote. “… I’m not sure why the FKT takes this route, it is definitely not the most direct. But I followed it, including to the Italian cross!

“… Rocked the descent from Hornlihutte, made one wrong turn I retraced my steps on, and made it back to the church for sub-7. Wish I had refilled food and water, but alas, no time for that!”

McCrystal’s LinkedIn profile lists her as a part-time instructor at the Capilano University School of Legal Studies, as well as a former senior associate for Borden Ladner Gervais LLP.

Skyrunning is an extreme form of mountain running. According to the International Skyrunning Federation, it is described as “running in the mountains above 2,000-meter altitude where the climbing difficulty does not exceed 11-degree grade and the incline is over 30 percent.”
